title: Horizontal vs Vertical Scaling
description: Understand when to scale horizontally vs vertically.

options.text: Vertical scaling requires application code changes
options.explanation: Vertical scaling (adding more CPU/RAM to existing server) typically requires NO code changes — the application runs on the same machine with more resources.

options.text: Horizontal scaling adds complexity around data consistency and session management
options.explanation: With multiple servers, you need load balancing, sticky sessions or externalized session stores, distributed caching, and strategies for data consistency across nodes.

options.text: Vertical scaling has no upper limit
options.explanation: Vertical scaling is bounded by the maximum hardware available — there's a ceiling on how much CPU/RAM a single machine can have.

options.text: Horizontal scaling is always cheaper than vertical scaling
options.explanation: For small to medium workloads, a single larger server can be cheaper than managing multiple smaller ones (no load balancer, simpler ops). Horizontal becomes cost-effective at scale.
